applies_to: Pedder juveniles in lake and refuge streams
role_in_model: Baseline annual survival of juvenile Pedder galaxias before threat-specific mortality terms are applied.
notes: Tightened from the first pass using life-history bounds plus the observed ability of the Oberon and Strathgordon populations to recruit and expand once predators are absent.

applies_to: Pedder adults in lake and refuge streams
role_in_model: Baseline annual survival of adult Pedder galaxias before threat-specific mortality terms are applied.
notes: Adult survival remains proxy-driven, but it is now better anchored by the documented persistence and growth of the insurance populations.

role_in_model: Annual maturation probability in the simplified juvenile-to-adult stage transition.
notes: Kept fairly tight because Pedder maturation at about two years is one of the better-supported life-history traits.

applies_to: Pedder adults contributing to annual recruitment
role_in_model: Pre-density-dependence fecundity term used in annual recruitment.
notes: Still interpreted as an effective annual recruitment term rather than literal realised egg production, but now narrowed to the better-supported middle of the reported fecundity range.

applies_to: Annual spawning allocation across lake and refuge compartments
role_in_model: Fraction of total spawning effort allocated to refuge-stream habitat.
notes: Shifted upward from the first pass because the species is consistently described as adfluvial and strongly linked to meandering stream habitat during reproduction.

applies_to: New recruits settling after annual recruitment
role_in_model: Fraction of new recruits settling into lake habitat rather than remaining in refuge streams.
notes: Broad by design because the exact juvenile settlement split is unknown, but the default now leans more strongly toward lake use during the boom phase.

applies_to: Threat-driven redistribution from lake to refuge streams
role_in_model: Annual fraction of Pedder state that can move from lake to refuge streams when combined threat pressure is high.
notes: Still one of the weakest process priors because the chronology implies redistribution or selective persistence, but not its annual rate.

parameter_group: Pedder density dependence or carrying terms
role_in_model: Scale parameter controlling the lake compartment carrying capacity under baseline conditions.
notes: Retained in index units, but widened slightly upward to allow the documented short-lived boom without forcing unrealistically large latent counts.

parameter_group: Pedder density dependence or carrying terms
role_in_model: Scale parameter controlling refuge-stream carrying capacity under baseline conditions.
notes: Still smaller than the lake compartment by default, but now better tied to the observed late persistence of a very small refuge network.

parameter_group: Pedder density dependence or carrying terms
role_in_model: Strength of density dependence acting on lake recruitment and survival.
notes: Remains a structural control needed to stop the upsurge phase producing implausible runaway Pedder abundance.

parameter_group: Pedder density dependence or carrying terms
role_in_model: Strength of density dependence acting on refuge recruitment and survival.
notes: Kept slightly stronger than the lake default because the refuge habitat is physically smaller and the Strathgordon case shows spawning bottlenecks matter.

applies_to: Brown trout state at inundation onset
role_in_model: Initial brown trout abundance / colonisation state at the start of the post-flood era.
notes: This remains indexed rather than absolute. The tighter lower end reflects the one-off stocking chronology and the assumption of a relatively small pre-boom founding state.

applies_to: Brown trout state response to fixed 1972 stocking event
role_in_model: Converts the fixed historical 350,000-fry stocking event into an increment in the trout abundance index.
notes: Still weak because the trout state is indexed rather than absolute; this parameter will remain a major uncertainty until stocking/growth records improve.

role_in_model: Annual growth rate of the trout abundance index in the absence of upsurge scaling.
notes: Broader than the direct Pedder evidence allows, but now more explicitly tuned to rapid early increase without assuming the stocking event alone caused permanent establishment.

role_in_model: Long-run carrying capacity of the trout abundance index after the trophic upsurge has faded.
notes: Still deliberately broad because there is no direct long-run trout abundance series for Lake Pedder after the trophy phase collapsed.

role_in_model: Strength with which trophic upsurge inflates trout effective carrying capacity during the early impoundment period.
notes: This is now one of the better-supported trout-mechanism priors because the post-flood productivity pulse, rapid trout growth, and 1977 peak all align.

role_in_model: Baseline piscivory pressure contributed by trout independent of the upsurge-driven overshoot phase.
notes: Kept broader than the upsurge-linked multiplier because the background predation signal is real but poorly quantified once the trophy phase fades.

role_in_model: Strength with which trophic upsurge amplifies trout piscivory during the early large-bodied phase.
notes: This prior is central to the transient overshoot story and is now more sharply separated from the baseline piscivory term.

role_in_model: Rate at which the upsurge-amplified trout piscivory modifier decays after the 1977 upsurge peak.
notes: This prior is constrained mainly by the known brevity of the trophy-trout phase rather than by a direct year-by-year trout time series.

role_in_model: Effect size linking trout abundance and piscivory to Pedder performance in lake habitat.
notes: Lake vulnerability remains heavily proxy-driven, with direct Pedder evidence on predation but no direct effect-size estimate. Ault and White 1994 remains the key Tasmanian anchor.

role_in_model: Effect size linking trout pressure to Pedder performance in refuge streams.
notes: This stays below the lake effect by default because the final refuge habitat offered cover, slow flow, and structural buffering, but not immunity.

role_in_model: Initial low abundance of climbing galaxias in the lake-connected system just after inundation.
notes: Kept low because climbing galaxias were not collected in the early sweep-net series and appear to have become important only later.

role_in_model: Initial climbing galaxias state in refuge-stream habitat after inundation.
notes: Set slightly above the lake initial state because later surveys show climbing galaxias becoming especially common in tributaries.

applies_to: Onset of climbing-galaxias expansion after inundation
role_in_model: Lag between system connection / inundation and the main climbing-galaxias expansion phase.
notes: The lag is one of the better-supported climbing parameters because the museum chronology clearly places the main shift after the initial Pedder decline.

role_in_model: Annual growth rate of climbing galaxias in lake habitat after the lag phase ends.
notes: Still weak because the lake growth rate is inferred indirectly from replacement timing rather than from a clean abundance time series.

role_in_model: Annual growth rate of climbing galaxias in refuge streams after the lag phase ends.
notes: Maintained above the lake default because climbing galaxias were relatively common in tributaries during the late decline phase.

role_in_model: Effect size linking climbing-galaxias abundance to Pedder performance in the lake compartment.
notes: Kept broad because the direct Pedder evidence supports a later contribution by climbing galaxias, but not a quantified lake effect size.

role_in_model: Effect size linking climbing-galaxias abundance to Pedder performance in refuge streams.
notes: Allowed to be as strong or stronger than the lake effect because late tributary coexistence with Pedder was poor and climbing galaxias likely blocked recovery there.

role_in_model: Peak amplitude of the deterministic early impoundment productivity pulse.
notes: The Lake 2001 littoral-fauna series and the cited 1977 fish peak make this one of the better-grounded structural priors in the whole model.

role_in_model: Exponential decay rate of the trophic-upsurge state after the fixed 1977 peak year.
notes: Tightened modestly to keep the upsurge influential through the late 1970s but largely faded by the late 1980s.

applies_to: Pedder annual recruitment and temporary lake productivity
role_in_model: Strength with which the trophic upsurge boosts Pedder recruitment and temporarily relaxes lake density pressure in the early post-flood years.
notes: The boom-phase evidence now supports a slightly firmer Pedder-productivity prior than in the first pass, even though the exact balance of recruitment and density-relief mechanisms remains unresolved.

applies_to: Pedder refuge-stream compartment and spawning sites
role_in_model: Baseline refuge-stream quality affecting survival and recruitment in the final natural refugia.
notes: Now better anchored by the shared lesson from Bonnet Bay, Oberon, and Strathgordon that suitable slow-flowing structured spawning habitat matters strongly.

role_in_model: Persistent habitat penalty applied to Pedder lake performance after the original shallow lake was lost.
notes: Retained as a real contributor rather than a null-only foil, but still not tight enough to overwhelm the biological interaction terms.

applies_to: Predation and competition effects in refuge streams
role_in_model: Multiplicative buffering of trout and climbing effects in refuge streams due to cover, slow flow, and stream structure.
notes: The structure of the final refuge habitat strongly implies buffering, but the magnitude still depends mostly on comparative trout-galaxiid studies.

role_in_model: Detection probability for occupancy-style comparisons in late historical surveys.
notes: Tightened slightly because the late surveys were repeated, targeted, and intensive enough that false absence cannot be treated as highly likely.

role_in_model: Scaling coefficient converting latent Pedder abundance to expected capture counts in electrofishing and repeated-trip surveys.
notes: Still weak because the count targets are sparse and heterogeneous, but the bound has been narrowed to avoid extremely low detectability masquerading as biological collapse.

role_in_model: Extra-Poisson dispersion term for count comparisons against sparse field observations.
notes: Kept broad because the calibration anchors are intentionally mixed and sparse; this remains a nuisance term likely to absorb observation heterogeneity.

role_in_model: Observation uncertainty around the museum-based Pedder-to-climbing dominance shift.
notes: Kept as a modestly informative observation term because the dominance switch is a strong signal, but it still comes from a curated museum-screening reconstruction rather than a routine survey series.

parameter_group: Pedder density dependence or carrying terms
role_in_model: Converts the index-scale carrying terms into model-internal latent count capacities for the Pedder states.
notes: Needed because Pedder states are latent counts while the carrying terms remain standardized indices; this parameter bridges those scales without forcing absolute historical census interpretation.

role_in_model: Lag in years before the post-inundation lake habitat penalty fully manifests in the Pedder dynamics.
notes: Introduced to let the model express the observed early post-flood boom before later habitat degradation dominates the lake compartment.
